paragraphs: If you don't, you'll see a Fathom panel also on your screen with a Start Recording button. Go ahead and click that button so that Fathom can join this meeting now.
Here is where the magic happens. Fathom has your back. You don't have to click a single button or take a single note.
Fathom will capture all of the important moments and action items and then will deliver them to your inbox within 30 seconds of the meeting ending.
You don't have to click a thing. But say that a really special moment on the call does happen that you know you want to go back and rewatch.
There's a highlight button on that Fathom panel. Go ahead and click that and you'll see it highlighted on the call recording page, which I'm also going to show you in a minute.
Anytime you want Fathom to stop recording, there is an end button on that Fathom panel. You can click that and Fathom will stop recording or when all participants.

Participants leave the meeting. Fathom will also stop recording. Once the call is done being recorded, that control panel will flip to a new screen and will have a big blue button that says view recording and summary.

When you click that button, it will take you to the call recording page. Alright, now go ahead, end this meeting, and then click that view recording and summary button, and I'll see you over on the call recording page.
But my video is not getting recorded. Okay, let me end this meeting.

templates.label: General
templates.title: How the recording workflow fits together
templates.overview: The presenter walks through the recording lifecycle: start capture, mark useful moments during the call, and return to the recording and summary when the conversation ends.

items.text: The host starts capture from the in-meeting recording panel.
Important moments can be marked during the call for faster review later.
The completed call leads into a recording and summary view.
The participant is asked to end the meeting and continue on the recording page.

templates.label: Sales / Customer
templates.title: A product walkthrough centered on less note-taking
templates.overview: The conversation frames the product around a simple customer outcome: preserve the important parts of a meeting without interrupting the discussion to take notes.

items.text: Automated capture is positioned as a way to stay present instead of taking notes.
Manual highlights give the user control over moments they already know they will revisit.
The post-call handoff puts the recording and summary behind one clear next step.
The participant reports that their video is not being recorded before ending the meeting.

templates.label: Recruiting / Interview
templates.title: Clear facilitation, with limited interview evidence
templates.overview: This was a product walkthrough rather than an interview. The template surfaces observable communication signals while avoiding unsupported judgments about experience, motivation, or role fit.

items.text: The presenter gives a direct first step and explains what the participant should expect next.
The workflow is explained in sequence from capture to post-call review.
The participant briefly raises a recording issue and then confirms they will end the meeting.
No role history, motivation, or hiring criteria are discussed in this conversation.
